question: Does weighing several context lengths together, with a model of repeated strings, give a smaller archive and a smaller complete size than DEFLATE on real structured input?
hypothesis: (a) mix+match archive bytes are smaller than DEFLATE archive bytes on english-prose, typescript-source and json-lockfile.
(b) mix+match total_declared_bytes is smaller than DEFLATE total_declared_bytes on json-lockfile.
prediction_not_part_of_the_hypothesis: mix+match loses to DEFLATE in total_declared_bytes on english-prose and typescript-source, because its 9,207-byte program is charged twice (18,414) against 2,590 for the DEFLATE worker, whose compressor lives uncounted in the Node runtime.
defeated_if: (a) fails on any of the three real inputs, or (b) fails, or any variant fails exact recovery on any input.

candidate.feature_disabled_variant: mix: the same program with the repeated-string input switched off

carried_reference: order1: the cycle 1 candidate, unchanged file
evaluator: src/core/school-prize.ts gradePrizeBundle and comparePrizeBundles, unchanged from c415ef861fc6066a3e741eaf0009992d6332d7bd
cost_definition: shared-program form: 2 * program bytes + archive bytes + option file bytes. mix and mixmatch are one program file. The Node runtime is not counted for any variant (program_format unqualified-source).
exposure: Before this plan was frozen the codec was run only on two files outside the study: docs/architecture.md and tests/extraction.test.ts at c415ef8 (archive 7,487 and 23,349 bytes with mix+match; DEFLATE 8,950 and 30,082), and on an empty file. No parameter was changed after those runs. The nine study inputs were seen in cycle 1 with other programs; this codec had not been run on them.
negative_controls: empty and short: fixed overhead dominates
one flipped archive bit must make the decoder exit non-zero with no output
